newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala crude oil exports slowed by strike.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala crude oil exports slowed by strike.

text.p: A strike by truckers who transfer Guatemala crude oil to shipping ports is dragging down the Central American nation's small crude exports, Rodolfo Sosa, president of Basic Petroleum International Ltd, said Monday.
The strike has partially interrupted oil shipments and work on a new pipeline, he said, although he did not know what percent of Basic's daily oil transport was affected by the strike.
Basic is the only oil producer in Guatemala and produces 20,000 barrels a day, most of which are exported.
Only 50 of 300 truck drivers employed by the company's trucking supplier are striking, according to Sosa.
He said the truckers are on strike because they fear the new pipeline, scheduled to be completed within days, will rob them of their jobs.
With the new pipeline, Basic will be able to move oil from the remote Xan oilfields to port on the Caribbean coast without using trucks.
Sosa said it will be up to the transport contractor for whom the drivers work, rather than Basic, to pay them severance pay when the pipeline is completed.
